mission_08: Impressive! You have implemented four advanced quantum data encoding strategies, each with distinct properties. Basis encoding is sparse and exact but uses the full Hilbert space inefficiently. Dense angle encoding doubles the feature capacity per qubit. Tree tensor encoding creates hierarchical correlations through structured entanglement, mimicking tensor network states. Hamiltonian encoding is the most expressive, simulating time evolution under a data-dependent Hamiltonian that includes both single-body and two-body interaction terms. The comparison reveals trade-offs: Hamiltonian encoding spreads amplitude across many basis states (high entropy, high expressivity), while basis encoding concentrates it in a single state (zero entropy, exact representation). Choosing the right encoding depends on the problem: simple data may need only angle encoding, while complex patterns benefit from Hamiltonian or tree tensor encodings.
